prompt: Give each constant of the Op enum its own implementation of the abstract apply method, then make compute delegate to it. ADD adds, SUB subtracts, MUL multiplies.
explanation: An enum can declare an abstract method, which forces every constant to provide its own implementation in a constant-specific class body. This turns a switch-on-enum into polymorphism: calling op.apply(a, b) dispatches to the right constant's code automatically. The compute method therefore needs no branching at all.
hints: Each constant can carry its own body in braces after its name, acting like a small anonymous subclass that overrides the abstract method for just that one constant.
ADD returns a + b, SUB returns a - b, MUL returns a * b.
compute needs no switch at all -- polymorphism does the work: return op.apply(a, b);
